messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Kickstart: Acceptance Pathway & MAP draft

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time last week. As promised, I pulled together a lightweight Mutual Action Plan that treats the MAP as an "Acceptance Pathway" — a short set of checkpoints aligned to your pilot acceptance criteria rather than an open-ended list. The goal is to keep evaluation focused and unblock procurement/IT quickly if the pilot hits the checkpoints.

Two items I attached/linked: 1) MAP_Kickstart_Template_v1.gdoc (editable) with suggested owners and week-by-week milestones, and 2) Acceptance_Pathway_Slides_v1.gslides with the pass/fail test cases we think are critical for a 30-day pilot.

Highlights in the draft:
- Week 0: Account & security onboarding (SOC2 evidence, data residency confirmation)
- Week 1: Feature smoke test & integration (sample workloads)
- Week 2: Latency/cost baseline and KV-cache validation
- Week 3: Quality check vs. your labeled prompts (thresholds included)
- Week 4: Acceptance sign-off + procurement/terms handoff

Can you review and tell us: 1) whether the acceptance tests map to what AcroHealth uses for pilots, and 2) who needs to be the sign-off approver on your side (technical + procurement)? If it's helpful, we can also run a 30-minute walkthrough of the MAP with your engineering and procurement teams.

Proposed next steps (if this looks good):
- T+2 business days: You review doc and add comments
- T+4 business days: 30-min walkthrough to align on pass/fail metrics
- T+10 business days: Pilot start

Link to docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uX-kickstart-map-draft

Thanks — looking forward to iterating.

—
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear structure. I skimmed the MAP and like the acceptance-pathway framing — helps keep internal stakeholders focused. A few quick notes from my side: 

- Security: SOC2 and proof of encryption at rest are must-haves. Can you point to a single artifact or page that summarizes the controls?
- Data residency: we need confirmation that data for the pilot will remain in US-east.
- Acceptance criteria: for the quality checks in Week 3, can we add a small subset of regulatory prompts we use internally? I'll upload 12 representative queries.
- Approvers: technical sign-off will be Rajiv (cc'd) and procurement will be our central procurement inbox (procurement@acrohealth.com).

Also, the 30-min walkthrough sounds good. We're available Wed 20th between 10–12 ET or Thu 21st after 2pm ET.

I'll add inline comments in the doc.

Attached the pilot controls summary (PDF stub in Drive). Short answers:
- SOC2: we can provide the SOC2 Type II summary/how it maps to pilot controls (drive link below).
- Encryption: data is encrypted at rest; pilot data will be hosted in a US-east tenant as requested.
- Integration: we recommend a small tokenized dataset for Week 1 to validate connectors; we'll provide a test harness.

Acceptance metric suggestion (we'll add to the doc after Emily uploads prompts):
- Quality: >= 85% pass on the 12 regulatory prompts (precision at top-1, manual review sample)
- Latency: P95 < 350ms on representative request mix
- Cost: unit cost within pilot budget (we'll provide simulated cost estimate during the walkthrough)

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/file/d/pilot-controls-summary.pdf
